title: Analytical and experimental investigation of neem‐coated cylindrical solar still for improved energy and exergy performance
content:
Abstract

Freshwater scarcity in coastal and dry regions remains a significant challenge, as the productivity of conventional solar stills is limited by low evaporation rates and inefficient interfacial heat transfer. This study analytically and experimentally investigates a cylindrical solar still (CSS) featuring a bio-derived neem leaf coating on the aluminium basin to enhance thin-film evaporation. Geometry-specific analytical expressions are formulated for instantaneous energy and exergy efficiencies, explicitly accounting for the curvature, basin–cover configuration, and heat transfer characteristics of the cylindrical enclosure. The model is validated through outdoor experiments conducted under tropical climatic conditions in Chennai, India, for three configurations: a conventional CSS, a CSS with a 50 μm neem coating, and a CSS with a 100 μm neem coating on the absorber basin. The 100 μm neem-coated configuration achieved the highest cumulative yield of 850 mL/day, resulting in an 11.11% improvement over the conventional still, while the 50 μm coating resulted in a 7.9% increase. Peak energy efficiencies of 63.1%, 64.5%, and 65.9% were observed for the conventional, 50 μm, and 100 μm coated stills, respectively. Peak exergy efficiencies increased from 3.45% for the conventional still to 4.12% and 4.47% for the coated cases. Analytical predictions closely matched experimental data, with correlation coefficients ranging from 0.93 to 0.96 and mean percentage deviations of ±8% or less. These findings indicate that neem-based surface modification improves surface wettability and thin-film evaporation behavior, enhancing evaporation dynamics and distillate productivity.
